speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help determine the cause of your fatigue and itching, have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes, or changes in the color of your urine or stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis and severe itching, I need to check for signs of jaundice such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, as well as any changes in stool color like pale or clay-colored stools. Do you also experience right upper quadrant abdominal pain or nausea?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis, the combination of jaundice and severe pruritus strongly suggests Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRCP is normal, we must rule out autoimmune liver diseases like Primary Biliary Cholangitis or Autoimmune Hepatitis, which can also present with cholestasis and fatigue. REQUEST TEST: Antimitochondrial Antibodies, Anti-Nuclear Antibodies, Liver Biopsy

text: Since the autoimmune markers are negative and PSC is ruled out, I need to investigate viral causes. Have you had any recent travel, exposure to blood products, or other risk factors for Hepatitis B or C?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your risk factors for blood-borne infections and the cholestatic pattern of liver injury, I need to rule out viral hepatitis. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis B Surface Antigen, Hepatitis C Antibody

speaker: Doctor
text: With viral and autoimmune causes largely ruled out, I suspect a medication-induced liver injury. What medications or supplements are you currently taking for your hypertension or ulcerative colitis?
